messages:
alice: Heads-up: multiple customers reporting 503s for hosted inference in us-west-2 since ~10:12UTC. CS escalations stacked. Saw repeated upstream worker exits (SIGSEGV) + GPU OOM in logs. Pushing stack/snippets below. Can SRE please triage?

support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1718200000, paging oncall.

deploy-bot: Detected 12 container restarts in pool gpu-pool-usw2-1 between 10:11:30 and 10:13:05. Autorestart triggered.

sre-oncall: I'm on it. Which service name / model? Any request IDs or example traces?

alice: Service: hosted-infer-prod, model: rwlm-13b-quant32. Sample request ids: req_34f9a2, req_34f9a8. From kube logs: ```Oct 12 10:12:17 runner[pid=7]: segfault at 0 ip 0x7f9c1a2b sp 0x7f9c... rax=0x0``` and shortly after ```nvml: GPU memory allocation failed: out of memory```

maya: I'm seeing the same in kernel logs on host gpunode-07: `kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus` then device reset. Looks like a hard GPU reset + driver noise.

devon: That matches a quant-swap path regression we rolled last night. We added a dynamic quantization path that touches KV cache allocation differently. If batch concurrency hits a threshold it can balloon memory during hot-swap. Short-term mitigation: reduce max_concurrency on the pool to 1 and force model fallback to fp16 variant.

sre-oncall: Doing that now: `curl -X POST https://controlplane/internal/pools/gpu-pool-usw2-1/config -d '{"max_concurrency":1}'` -> applied. Triggering fallback routing for active requests to dedicated-cpu-small.

jamal: CS: Customers impacted include acme-inc and pulseai. They're asking for ETA and want billing paused for failed requests. Can we bulk-refund or mark those tokens as failed?

alice: Filing billing hold request with finance+billing. For now add a customer tag so we don't bill for requests between 10:11:30-10:13:30 in the affected pools.

maya: I'm collecting coredumps and kernel traces. Commands run: `kubectl -n hosted-infer logs pod/gpu-runner-7 -c runner --previous` and `sudo journalctl -k -b --since "10:00" | grep NVRM`. Found `segfault` in `/opt/infer/runner` with backtrace symbolizing to `attention_kernel.cu:line 214`.

devon: Can you grab the exact backtrace? If it's the same segfault path we saw in internal CI then revert of the quant swap build (release 2026.03.11-quant-v2) should stop crashes. I'll prepare a hotfix rollback.

sre-oncall: Reverting runtime release on those hosts now (rolling restart). `orchestrator rollback --release 2026.03.10-stable --pool gpu-pool-usw2-1` -> in progress.

deploy-bot: Rolling restart started for 6 nodes in gpu-pool-usw2-1. Expected 9m.

alice: CS update posted to customers: "We're investigating a runtime crash causing 503s. We've engaged SRE and are rolling a quick rollback; we'll follow up with incident summary and credits if necessary." :white_check_mark:

maya: After draining one node and reproing, I captured a small repro that reliably triggers: run a long streaming request (context ~60k tokens) with concurrent embed prefetch -> GPU mem spike then segfault. Dump attached to incident.

devon: Hotfix rollback accepted. Patch in QA to guard the dynamic allocation code path. Will open PR to add thresholds around KV prefetch sizing.

sre-oncall: Pool stabilized after rollback and roll restarts; error rate dropped to baseline by 10:21UTC. Fallback routing handled remaining in-flight requests. Marking incident as mitigated.

jamal: Thanks — CS will coordinate credits and customer comms. Please add a short timeline for the postmortem.

alice: Noted. I'll start the postmortem draft and include repro steps + suggested runbook changes: auto-fallback on nvml reset, max_concurrency caps for quant-enabled pools, pause billing for detected 5xx bursts.

maya: Follow-up actions assigned: collect full coredumps (storage link: https://internal/redwood/incidents/1718200000/dumps), add kernel-level alert for Xid 79, and add automated rollback on repeated segfaults.

devon: I'll open a PR referencing INC-2026-1718200000 with the code fix and add a unit test for memory prefetch cap.

sre-oncall: Closing thread for immediate triage. Follow-up meeting at 14:00UTC today. :calendar:
